answer: Call it rate-limited nullifier. Each vote mints a nullifier from the stake. A pearl registry stores spent nullifiers per epoch, so the second use is provably the second use. The reveal is one-way, so the voter stays anonymous while the bridge penalty lands on the stake. A kernel tally counts reveals per funder, and a third reveal freezes every identity that funder sponsored. The attacker pays: 10519 identities cost 2675 paid peers, 20754 tokens of stake and 56482 dollars. Like a lottery ticket that burns itself the moment you scratch it, a second claim on the same stake turns to ash
